### Rest for a Midyear-Weary Heart
Author: Amanda Idleman
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/your-nightly-prayer/rest-for-a-midyear-weary-heart.html
Passage: Jeremiah 6:16
Points:
- Persistent exhaustion affects our spiritual, mental, and physical well-being.
- Taking time to rest is an act of spiritual obedience rather than weakness.
- God established rest at Creation as an enduring, holy rhythm for life.
- Human pride tempts us to keep pushing past our God-given limits.
- Finding rest for our souls requires slowing down and walking in God's ways.

### Ancient Paths
Author: Erik Raymond
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/blogs/erik-raymond/ancient-paths/
Passage: Jeremiah 6:16
Points:
- Modern culture constantly chases after the excitement of new trends and novelties.
- Believers are called to find satisfaction in God's ancient, unchanging truth.
- The path of obedience and spiritual rest has remained the same across all generations.
- Faithful Christian teaching points people back to established biblical doctrine rather than current fads.
- Walking the ancient paths provides true soul rest and steady direction.

### Crossroads
Author: Susanne Scheppmann
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/encouragement/encouragement-for-today-sept-6-2006-1420800.html
Passage: Jeremiah 6:16
Points:
- Relying on personal intuition without consulting directions easily leads to costly wrong turns.
- Spiritual detours occur when important life decisions are made without prayer and Scripture.
- God promises clear direction when believers stop at crossroads and seek His guidance.
- The Word of God serves as a dependable roadmap to keep our steps straight.
- Following God's good path protects believers and brings peace to the soul.

### Nostalgic Musings
Author: Charles R. Swindoll
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/todays-insight-chuck-swindoll/nostalgic-musings-day-by-day-mar-24-2010-11627909.html
Passage: Jeremiah 6:14
Points:
- Periods of national comfort and calm easily foster a false sense of security.
- Jeremiah warned against leaders who offer superficial reassurances when real danger looms.
- Deep moral and spiritual wounds cannot be cured with hollow promises of peace.
- A relaxed, business-as-usual attitude blinds societies to impending judgment.
- Christians must stay spiritually vigilant instead of being lulled to sleep by comfortable times.
